transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-12 14:00 EDT
Duration: 48 mins
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE); Evan Chu (Redwood SE); Tom Reyes (CISO, Abbey Financial); Sara Lin (Head Cloud Eng); Ben Ortiz (VP Product)

Summary (auto): quick discovery to validate regulatory constraints and preferred deployment mode; request for security artifacts + network diagram; schedule tech deep dive.

00:00 Maya: okay hi everyone thanks for joining, this is Maya from Redwood Inference, I'm the account owner for Abbey, with me is Evan our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
00:05 Tom: hey Maya, thanks, doing well. we got about 45 minutes, wanted to go over our residency and compliance concerns before we move to a pilot.
00:12 Evan: great, can you give us a little context on current stack and what you're trying to protect?
00:18 Sara: sure. we run most stuff in AWS us-east-1 and we have teams in EU (Frankfurt) for euro customers. primary concern is PII and financial data—transactional metadata, acct numbers get masked but some workflows touch raw data.
00:28 Ben: timeline is tight, Q2 pilot ideally, but compliance has to sign off.
00:33 Maya: totally makes sense. so two axes i want to cover: where data physically resides and what logs / telemetry you allow Redwood to retain. Also key management and access controls.
00:41 Tom: exactly. regarding residency, for EU citizens we need data to remain in EU. For US customers we prefer us-only. also legal wants the option for a private deployment if hosted can't satisfy logs restrictions.
00:52 Evan: okay. with Redwood Hosted we operate region-backed endpoints; EU requests can be served from our eu-central region. For stronger guarantees we offer Redwood Dedicated—reserved GPU capacity in a region with stricter tenancy—and Redwood Private for VPC/on-prem where you control the network.
01:05 Tom: can you clarify differences in audit logging? legal is worried about logs that include prompts or partial responses—those are considered regulated.
01:14 Evan: good question. hosted by default retains telemetry for service quality but we can configure retention windows and enable prompt redaction. For Dedicated we can restrict retention to 30 days or disable certain telemetry; for Private the control plane can be customer-managed and you can opt to not send logs to Redwood's central store.
01:30 Sara: how mature is the redaction? we can't have accidental prompt text in logs—especially sensitive tokens or account numbers.
01:36 Evan: we have automatic PII heuristics and can add custom regex-based scrubbers. caveat: ASR/transcription artifacts sometimes mis-detect, we'll need to test on your sample data.
01:46 Tom: KMS question—do you support customer-managed keys or HSM? regulatory will want keys they control.
01:52 Maya: yes, we support BYOK via KMS integrations; for Private deployments we can integrate with your KMS or HSM so keys never leave your control. For Hosted we support CMEK for certain plans but the master key lifecycle is managed by you.
02:07 Ben: latency tradeoffs? Private sounds heavy and maybe higher latency for multi-region users.
02:12 Evan: correct—Private gives control but you bear the infra latency tradeoffs. Dedicated in-region usually hits better predictability while keeping lower latency than cross-region Private. We can also do smart routing: EU requests to EU Dedicated or Private, US to US.
02:26 Tom: GDPR requires a data processing agreement and potentially SCCs for transfers. do you have a DPA and standard contract language?
02:32 Maya: yes, we'll include our DPA and SCCs in the security pack. we'll also surface SOC 2 Type II and our HIPAA attestation artifacts.
02:40 Sara: logging restrictions—can you completely disable request/response logging? or is there always some metadata?
02:46 Evan: there's always some minimal telemetry for platform health (error rates, token counts) but request/response bodies can be suppressed or redacted. for Dedicated we can minimize retained payloads; for Private you control whether payloads are stored.
02:59 Tom: what about backups and logs stored in third-party analytics—like if you forward to datadog or S3? we must prevent that for certain data classes.
03:06 Maya: forwarding integrations are opt-in and can be disabled per account. in enterprise contracts we can lock that down.
03:12 Ben: i remember reading about KV cache—how does that interact with persistence?
03:16 Evan: KV cache (we sometimes say K V cache in docs) is an in-memory accelerator; it doesn't persist to disk unless configured for durability. for Private we can keep it entirely in-memory; for Dedicated we can configure purge intervals.
03:28 Sara: any certifications that matter for finance? SOC 2 is baseline, ISO 27001 would help; for payments we may need FFIEC guidance alignment.
03:36 Maya: SOC 2 Type II is available; we're actively pursuing ISO but we'll share current status. we also have customer audit support and can provide architecture diagrams for auditors.
03:47 Tom: for HIPAA—some of our partners are in healthcare. do you sign a BAA?
03:51 Maya: yes, we can sign a BAA for covered workloads; we'll include the BAA template in the pack.
03:58 Ben: ok interesting. pricing—Dedicated seems pricey; can you provide cost per 8xA100 equivalent or something?
04:05 Evan: yes we'll provide a breakdown: reserved GPU pool pricing, expected throughput, token unit economics and pilot discounts.
04:12 Tom: about private deployment: network requirements—do you support VPC peering only or transit gateway and on-prem?
04:18 Evan: we support VPC peering and AWS PrivateLink patterns; for on-prem we support air-gapped appliance deployments. we'll share sample network diagrams and firewall rules.
04:29 Sara: for the pilot we need a matrix: in-scope data types, required controls, who's the approver. can you propose a pilot scope?
04:36 Maya: yes. suggested pilot: 4-week POC in EU region on Dedicated with prompt redaction enabled and telemetry minimized; we run a quality baseline and regressions on your prompts, and provide security audit artifacts.
04:48 Tom: who will be involved from redwood side in the deep dive?
04:51 Maya: Evan will lead the technical deep dive plus a solutions architect and account manager for procurement.
04:58 Ben: any blockers for us to test quickly? we need sample contract language for legal and a security package upfront.
05:03 Maya: we'll send the security pack (SOC2, DPA, HIPAA, network diagram) and draft pricing.
05:09 Tom: one more thing—data residency for backups and disaster recovery. backups must remain in-region and we need the option to encrypt snapshots with our keys.
05:18 Evan: for Dedicated we can ensure backups are region-scoped and encrypted with CMEK; for Private you control snapshot lifecycle.
05:26 Sara: okay that's helpful. i have a granular question on log retention windows—what's the minimum?
05:30 Evan: for hosted the default is 90 days, but enterprise/DEDICATED can go down to 30 days, and Private you can set to zero retained payloads. metadata like request counts will stay for operational reasons but can be aggregated.
05:45 Tom: any chance to run a small benchmark for PII detection and redaction before pilot starts?
05:49 Evan: yes, send a sanitized sample set and we'll run it through our scrubbers and show false positive/negative rates.
05:55 Ben: timeline: if we get artifacts this week we can start legal review and get procurement moving.
06:00 Maya: will do. Alex—sorry alex? (crosstalk)
06:03 Tom: no worries.
06:05 Maya: wrapping up—recap of action items and next steps?
06:08 Maya: i'll send SOC2, DPA, HIPAA, security pack + draft SOW; Evan will send network diagram and pilot pricing; Tom will share in-scope data list. we'll schedule the tech deep dive for next week.
06:20 Tom: yep that works. thanks everyone.
06:23 Sara: thanks all.
06:25 End of transcript.
